mechanism_narrative: A sudden increase in the Consumer Price Index (CPI) above 2% annualized signals inflationary pressure, leading to tighter monetary policy expectations and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or CPIAUCSL annualized increase > 2% does not correlate with subsequent tightening actions by the Fed.

mechanism_narrative: A significant drop in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) below 5% signals a tightening labor market, which increases wage pressures and leads to higher inflation expectations, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or UNRATE < 5% does not correlate with subsequent inflationary pressures.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) signals strong consumer demand, which boosts corporate earnings and leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in > 40% of periods with increasing RSAFS, or RSAFS growth does not correlate with earnings growth.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in industrial production (INDPRO) signals weakening supply-side fundamentals, which leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or INDPRO decline does not correlate with subsequent economic slowdown.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is below 1% and the unemployment rate (UNRATE) is above 8%, it signals an accommodative monetary policy in a weak labor market, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
regime_hint: accommodative policy in weak labor market
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in > 40% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or the combination of low FEDFUNDS and high UNRATE does not correlate with subsequent equity performance.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) combined with a decrease in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) signals a strengthening labor market, which boosts consumer confidence and spending, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 5-day returns in > 40% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or the combination of PAYEMS increase and UNRATE decrease does not correlate with subsequent equity performance.

mechanism_narrative: A significant increase in housing starts (HOUST) signals a strong demand for new homes, which boosts related sectors and leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 60-day returns in > 40% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or HOUST increase does not correlate with subsequent economic growth.

mechanism_narrative: When GDP (GDPC1) growth slows to less than 1% quarter-over-quarter and industrial production (INDPRO) is stagnant, it signals a weakening supply-side economy, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 QoQ growth < 1% and INDPRO YoY growth < 1%
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or the combination of slow GDPC1 growth and stagnant INDPRO does not correlate with subsequent equity performance.
